# Spec: Manter o plano de fechamento auditável no corpus federado

## 1. Intent

### Goal
Permitir que a captura e a auditoria concluam o plano de fechamento do corpus Harne8 medido, com limites explícitos por operação.

### Business value
Com Harne8 em `dacd8e8e` e pose-dist em `903b1b10`, o plano dos hooks atinge 40.000 observações e perde o veredito de frescor. A comparação com a árvore materializada consome 13.440 observações e a verificação de materiais federados esgota o orçamento compartilhado. A medição diagnóstica contou 41.143 observações, 285.047.615 bytes de insumos e 6.101.031 bytes de metadados para a passagem de captura completa dos hooks.

### Constraints
Preservar a cobertura da árvore, o orçamento total entre roots, os limites independentes de bytes e metadados e o bloqueio de operações com insumos desconhecidos.

### Non-goals
Mudar a política de revisão, o pin do Harne8 ou a descoberta de specs.

## 2. Requirements

- R1: Capture, audit and proof recheck shall admit up to 50,000 observations per operation, including directory entries under the existing shared accounting.
- R2: An operation exceeding the observation, byte or metadata limit shall keep freshness unknown and refuse to authorize a transition.
- R3: The three outstanding Harne8 plans shall report current read-view freshness against the indexed candidate corpus without skipping tree, policy or federated input checks.

… r não repara nada (spec `pose-journal-checkpoint-and-lock-recovery`); `open` é preview até `--apply`. Os alvos são qualificados com o project id atual; quando ele é derivado do nome do diretório (sem `.pose/project.json`, `POSE_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID` ou vínculo em `POSE_PROJECT_ROOTS`), `open --apply` avisa (no stderr com `--json`), porque um checkout com outro nome registraria outro projeto, e o snapshot das obrigações lista a mesma limitação. Uma resolução nomeia o `--request-digest` que responde e a `--expected-revision` que leu, traz uma `--idempotency-key` (retry não grava de novo, a mesma chave com outro conteúdo é recusada, uma segunda resposta contra a mesma revisão é recusada) e vem de um ator que detém o papel destinatário em `.pose/policy/actions.json` (`{"schema_version":1,"roles":{"maintainer":["human:<nome>"]},"identity_assurance":"declared|verified"}`); em `verified` exige `--claim <arquivo>` com uma claim Ed25519 de um emissor fixado na policy de review, vinculada a projeto, audience, digest da solicitação, principal e resposta (um principal humano também exige `human_authority_issuers`). Respondida não é satisfeita: aprovação recusada, aceite rejeitado ou operação externa falha deixam a condição sem atendimento. O solicitante pode cancelar a própria pergunta; uma dispensa exige a autoridade destinatária e um motivo. Solicitações abertas são projetadas como obrigações `actor-action` em `state --attention` e `pose_obligations`; o MCP abre solicitações com `pose_action_open` (classe de risco `governance-write`, preview a menos que `apply` seja true) e as lê com `pose_action_requests`; `pose_action_resolve` (spec `pose-mcp-action-resolve-signed-only`, `governance-write`) registra uma resposta só com a prova do principal — assinatura de uma chave registrada para ele, ou a claim de um emissor confiável — e recusa resposta declarada sob qualquer garantia; o preview devolve a declaração a assinar e o comando `ssh-keygen`.

Scopes explícitos substituem esse padrão: uma request de alpha pode restringir beta sem bloquear alpha. Artifact inteiro nomeado é restrição inteira; qualificação não o torna parcial. CLI aceita `--effect-json '{"phase":"start","mode":"block","scope":["xref:project/spec:beta"]}'`; MCP `effects` aceita esse objeto junto de strings legadas `"start:block"`. Targets e subjects resolvem o tuple projeto/artifact/kind/ID; subject é relido no artifact registrado. Sob agency readiness adotado, novas aprovações e aceitações exigem `--subject` / `subject` explícito; journals legados sem binding permanecem intactos e declaram que a resposta não detecta mudança de conteúdo. Criação e transições com policy off preservam os padrões existentes. Revisar compatibilidade na release; esta implementação não adota policy.

Closing spec `pose-closeout-review-policy-by-cost-benefit`, `pose index` in a
fresh clone and then in the maintainer checkout refused the pose-dist corpus:
`index.delivery-integrity` exceeded the captured-input budget and
`index.generate` was left without a complete observation. Measured with a Git
shim on the real builder: the change sets of every spec read `git show
--binary` for 2,451 distinct trailer commits, 492 MB of Git output in the
capture (the final audit reads it again under its own budget), plus the file
inputs of the generation, so the operation needed more than 512 MiB. Nothing
was truncated; the refusal was correct. Raise the captured-input budget to
1 GiB, for capture and audit alike, and keep every other limit, including the
512 MiB executable-hash bound of D9. Observations retain their bytes, so the
operation may now hold up to 1 GiB of captured input in memory. This
recalibration buys headroom, not a scaling property: the corpus grows with
every attributed commit. The structural fix, retaining only a digest for pure
reads of immutable Git objects whose bytes a producer only hashes, is a
follow-up of that spec, and a further raise again requires a measured
reassessment.

# Review: spec:pose-closeout-read-view-covers-the-federated-corpus

decision: approved

The change is one shared constant, raised from 40,000 to 50,000, with a new boundary test, an ADR amendment and four matching doc copies. I found two low-severity documentation gaps and no blockers.

My own run of `pose validate --strict` did not pass in this sandbox. It exited 1 for both the module and the workspace: 11 tests failed and 1 timed out. All of them are runtime, delegate, journey or file-mode tests, and they fail the same way when I put the old 40,000 limit back through a build overlay. So the sandbox causes them, not this change. Two facts support marking `validate` passed anyway:
- The bundle seals passing runs of those same checks.
- That evidence is bound to `83334d02`, and `pose-mcp` hasn't changed between that commit and `d0d9980c`.

## What I checked
- **One limit everywhere:** the constant `governanceReadViewMaxRecords` (`governance_read_view.go:24`) bounds capture (`:630`, `:784-803`), audit (`:180`, `:197`, which includes directory entries), proof replay (`:2131`, `:2410-2470`) and the index traversal check (`index_generation.go:1080`). The other limits are unchanged: 512 MiB retained input, 16 MiB metadata and 8 GiB streamed (`governance_read_view_stream.go:27`).
- **Targeted tests:** the spec's test commands pass with `-race`:
  - `TestGovernanceReadViewObservationLimit`, the two-root test and the probe capacity test.
  - The wider `GovernanceReadView|ReviewOperationView|IndexFederatedMaterial` set.
- **Mutation check:** with the limit reverted to 40,000 through `go test -overlay` (no repository edits), `TestGovernanceReadViewObservationLimit` fails with "capture refused record 40001". The two-root overflow test still passes because it is written relative to the constant. That confirms the implementer's claim that each root fits alone and their total is refused.
- **Tools:**
  - `artifact-check --strict`: exit 0. Its 982 findings are all orphan warnings across the repository, none from this scope.
  - `surface-check --strict`: exit 0, 0 findings.
  - `assess design`: reproduced the sealed digest `295cfa74…`.
  - `assess integrate`, `tech-debt` and `discover`: ran but couldn't save their output, because the review worktree is read-only.
- **Docs:** `POSE.md`, the pt-BR copy and both scaffold copies all say 50,000.
- **Committed validation:** `.pose/results/delivery-validation.json` is bound to `git_head` `83334d02`.

## Criteria
All 15 are **passed**. The evidence and reasons are in the block below.

## Structural fact
- SD-2d7579b1 (ADR amendment) → **D1**, the decision to recalibrate the limit to 50,000 in that ADR.

## Defects
| id | severity | file:line | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | low | `.pose/reports/closeout-read-view-federated-corpus.json:73` | The R3 report doesn't name the engine commit or binary that produced it, so the manual evidence can't be tied to the reviewed code. I couldn't re-run it either, because the Harne8 corpus isn't available here. |
| F2 | low | `.pose/adr/2026-11-03-governance-reads-use-bounded-operation-scoped-views.md:378` | The amendment calls 50,000 the "capture and audit" limit. It doesn't mention that proof replay and the index traversal check share the same constant, so that traversal bound also went up. |

Both are follow-ups with an action, owner and review date, so they are accepted as low risks.

## Cleanup
I waited for all test, build and background jobs to finish. As the final command, inside the sandbox, I ran `go clean -cache` and removed the leftover `go-build*` directories under `$GOTMPDIR`. Both succeeded, and none remain.
